desk.headline: Adjusted EPS $5.04 vs $1.54 a year ago, beat; Q4 spot rates booked so far at record highs, no formal guidance
results: Revenue rose 61% to $369.2m as spot tanker rates stayed near records; Suezmax rates averaged about $106,400 a day, more than triple a year ago.
Adjusted net income was $175.8m ($5.04 a share), down from $193.6m in Q2 after two ship sales and slightly lower rates.
GAAP profit of $195.2m included a $22.9m gain on selling a VLCC tanker.
Nine-month adjusted profit of $497.7m is already close to the company's record full year (2023).
Cash and short-term investments reached $1.42bn; the fixed $0.25 dividend is payable 4 Dec.

guidance.summary: No formal earnings guidance. So far in Q4 the company has booked Suezmax spot days at $272,000 a day (63% fixed) and Aframax/LR2 at $208,300 (53% fixed), and says it is positioned for its best-ever Q4 and full year.

points: The CEO pointed to conflicts in the Middle East Gulf, Ukraine and the Red Sea as keeping oil flows disrupted and voyages longer.
High refining margins and supply-chain detours are adding to tanker demand; mid-sized rates hit records in October.
Fleet renewal continues: four newbuilds ordered for 2030 delivery, plus options on two more Suezmaxes and a modern MR tanker purchase.
Management warned that rising tanker deliveries and the fate of the shadow fleet could weigh on supply balance in coming years.
call.source: CEO commentary and market section in the results release (6-K); no call coverage found

watch: Whether record Q4 spot bookings hold for the remaining unfixed days.
Use of the $1.4bn cash pile: fixed dividend only so far, alongside newbuild payments.
Geopolitical shifts (Hormuz, Red Sea) that could quickly change tanker rates.

sources.title: Teekay Tankers A Aktie: Q3-Gewinn übertrifft Erwartungen — Goldesel, 11 Nov 2026
